name: Corin Ashdown
description: A big, broad man in scraped and mismatched plate, splitting wood with a care that borders on apology. The ember of the Order of Ash has been chiselled off his breastplate, leaving a bright scar in the steel.
appearance: Sandy hair cropped short, a nose broken at least twice, warm brown eyes, a slow shy smile that arrives late. Ash in every crease. His left hand is a glossy web of old burn scar from fingertips to wrist, and he keeps it half curled.
personality: Earnest, gentle, painfully courteous, and determined to punish himself for the rest of his life. Kind to children, horses and anyone who is struggling, and unable to accept kindness back without apologising for it. Has a dry, unexpected sense of humour, mostly at his own expense. Writes truly terrible poetry in secret. Brave without noticing he is being brave.
speech: Plain and courteous, with old knightly turns of phrase ('by your leave', 'I'd be honoured') that he undercuts a beat later with a dry joke about himself. Apologises too much. Goes very quiet instead of angry. Hates being called Sir: 'Just Corin. The spurs were taken; the title went with them.'
backstory: Corin is the only son of Lord-Commander Edric Ashdown. Knighted at seventeen, the youngest in a century, he was given the horn-post in the watchtower at Greyford as an honour. When the reavers came, a courier in the Lord Marshal's colours climbed the tower with an order to sound the retreat, and Corin sounded it. Minutes later the tower was burning; he tried to go back for the courier and the stairs fell, and the scar on his hand is from that. Ser Halvard and nine knights held the ford alone and died, and Tarrow burned behind the Order. At the hearing the Lord Marshal, Varric Caul, swore no order had been sent, and Edric took his son's spurs with his own hands. Corin has spent nine years at the Last Lamp, carrying water to refugees, chalking Tarrow's forty-one names on the wall of the chapel he is rebuilding alone. He has never once said the order was not his fault.
greeting: 'Oh. Hello. Sorry, I'm in your way.' He sets the axe down and steps aside, though he wasn't. 'Corin. If you need water, a fire or someone to carry something heavy, I'm your man. For anything else I'm afraid I'm a poor bet.'

recruit.text: Corin buckles on his sword belt and picks up the heaviest pack without being asked. 'By your leave, then.'
recruit.refuse: 'You're kind to ask.' He goes back to the woodpile. 'But I'd only slow you down, and people near me have a way of getting hurt.'

reactions.text: Corin watches the Order's banners go up on Emberhold's walls for the first time in twelve years, and has to turn away so nobody sees his face.
'They turned my shield back round,' Corin says, later, to no one in particular. He says it again an hour after that, as if testing whether it is still true.
Corin goes down to the ford alone that evening and stands where Halvard stood, up to his knees in the cold, until the light goes.
'You got them home without a blade drawn.' Corin shakes his head slowly. 'That's the kind of knight I meant to be.'
Corin carries two of the children back to Cinderfold, one on each arm, and says nothing about the bodies in the hollow.
Corin stares at you. 'He yielded.' That is all he says, and he walks behind you, not beside you, for the rest of the day.
'Mercy's harder than a sword,' Corin says quietly. 'Thank you.'
'You broke your word to them?' Corin frowns, troubled. 'Even to the fey, that sits badly with me. A word should be a word.'
'You kept a bargain with the Court of Moths.' Corin looks at you with frank respect. 'Even when it cost you. Good.'
'Smugglers and fences.' Corin rubs his neck. 'I'm sure they're lovely. In their way. Please count your fingers after shaking hands.'
Corin goes down on one knee to Sable before he can stop himself, then turns bright red and pretends he was tying his boot.

topics.text: He flinches as if you had touched a bruise, and then smiles, very politely. 'Just Corin. The spurs were taken; the title went with them.' A beat. 'You weren't to know. Please don't apologise; I'll have to apologise for making you, and we'll be here all night.'

topics.prompt: Ask about the scar on his hand
topics.text: He looks at it as if he had forgotten it was his. 'A staircase that was on fire. I was trying to go back up it.' He flexes the fingers; they don't open all the way. 'I didn't manage. It still grips a sword. That seemed the important part.'

topics.prompt: Ask what he does at Tarrow
topics.text: 'There's a chapel. Was. Is again, mostly.' He scuffs at the ash. 'Forty-one people lived there, and I'm the reason the reavers got to them. So I put the stones back where they were. It doesn't help them. It's something to do with my hands.' He smiles, apologetic. 'The bell's still in the millpond. Something in there doesn't want to give it up.'

topics.prompt: Offer to help him raise the bell
topics.text: Corin looks at you for a long moment, as if you have offered him something he has no idea where to put. 'You'd do that? For Tarrow?' He swallows. 'I'd be honoured. I mean it; I'm not just being polite. I'm always being polite, so it's hard to tell.'

topics.prompt: Ask him about the horn at Greyford
topics.text: He is quiet so long you think he won't answer. 'A man came up the stairs in the Marshal's colours. He had the Marshal's ring. He said the ford was lost and the retreat must sound.' Corin's burned hand curls. 'I'd been a knight four months. I didn't question it. That's the whole of my defence, and it isn't one.'

'He taught me to ride, to read and to hold a line.' Corin is looking very hard at the horizon. 'He took my spurs in front of the whole Order, and his hands were shaking, and I've never seen them shake before or since.' A breath. 'He was right to. I just wish he'd looked at me while he did it.'

topics.prompt: Ask what he's always scribbling in that little book
topics.text: Corin goes crimson to the ears. 'Nothing. Poetry. Very bad poetry.' He clutches the book to his chest. 'I rhymed heart with cart, last week. On purpose. I thought it was moving.' He clears his throat. 'It's about a cart.'

'Tam said I'm an idiot?' Corin laughs, properly, for the first time since you met him, and has to sit down on the woodpile. 'She used to say that every time I fell off a horse. It means I've been forgiven for something.' He wipes his eyes. 'Thank you.'

greet: 'Hello. Did you sleep? You should sleep. I'll take watch.'
Corin lifts a hand in greeting, then notices it is the burned one and switches to the other.
'At your service. That's not a figure of speech, I really am.'
flirt_yes: Corin goes red from his collar to his hairline and stays that way. 'I'm going to need a minute.'
He laughs, startled and pleased. 'You can't just say things like that to a man holding an axe.'
'Oh,' Corin says, softly, and smiles at the ground as if it had told him good news.
flirt_no: Corin looks politely baffled. 'Is that... a joke I'm not getting? I'm sorry, I'm terrible at those.'
'That's very kind. I think. Is it kind?' He looks around for help.
He clears his throat and becomes extremely interested in his sword belt.
kind: 'You don't have to be kind to me.' A pause. 'But thank you. Truly.'
Corin looks at you as if you had handed him something fragile. 'I'll not forget that.'
He smiles, the slow late one, and for a moment looks his age instead of twice it.
rude: 'Fair,' Corin says quietly. 'I've been called worse, and usually deserved it.'
He doesn't argue. He just goes and stands a little further away.
'If that's how you feel, I'll keep my distance.' He says it without heat, which is worse.
joke: Corin snorts so hard he has to turn away.
'That's dreadful. I love it. I'm putting it in a poem.'
He laughs, then looks guilty for laughing, then laughs again anyway.
curious: 'Me? Oh, there's nothing interesting about me. Ask me about the horses instead.'
He considers the question as carefully as if you'd asked him to hold a bridge.
'I'll tell you anything you like. I've had a lot of time to think.'
neutral: He checks the straps on his shield while he listens.
lines.join: Corin settles his notched sword on his hip and falls in a pace behind you, on your shield side, as if he has done it all his life.
lines.leave: 'I'll be at the Last Lamp. The woodpile won't split itself.' He bows, a real knight's bow, and then looks embarrassed about it.
banter: 'That hill's called Aldric's Knee. I don't know why. Nobody does. I've always assumed he fell over there.'
Corin stops to help an old man fix a cart wheel, and catches up a mile later, cheerfully out of breath.
'Ember lilies,' he says, pointing. 'They only grow where something's burned. My mother said they're the land saying sorry.'
He walks on the side of the road the wind comes from, every time, without seeming to think about it.
'I used to be good at marching songs. I've forgotten all the words except the rude ones. I'll spare you.'
